**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow prepositions before recurring payment dates**

Fresh evidence beyond the repaired no-preposition layouts is that `王甲工资于每月15日发放` and `王甲工资在每月15日发放` still receive `source_relation_unresolved`: this recurring branch requires the left side to be exactly the wage noun, although the calendar-date branch below accepts the same bounded `于`/`在` bridge. These common recurring payment schedules should pass the same-worker attribution gate.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fold traditional glyphs in payment deadlines**

Fresh evidence beyond the previously repaired traditional date cues is that valid deadlines such as `王甲工資應於2026年1月15日前給付` and `...支付完畢` still fail attribution while their `给付`/`完毕` equivalents pass. Because the date detection fold omits `給` and `畢`, the deadline layout adds `source_relation_unresolved`, preventing these traditional payment dates from being used.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude the anchored subject from qualifier detection**

When a worker's name ends with a qualifier character, the full quote prefix is mistaken for an amount modifier: runtime validation of `王近工资4000元` with subject `王近`, or `王约工资4000元` with subject `王约`, changes the exact `4000.00` to `approximate` and adds `source_amount_context_mismatch`, while `王甲工资4000元` remains exact. Strip only the already anchored complete subject before applying the prefix qualifier grammar so characters inside a person's name cannot suppress a valid amount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require complete slash denominators to match rate units**

For slash rates, `suffix[1]` captures the entire letter sequence, but this prefix match accepts only its beginning as the supported unit. Consequently `normalizeMoneyValueV4('4000元/月亮')`, `4000元/月份`, and `4000元/小时候` all return exact `4000.00` instead of rejecting the attached unsupported denominator; a rate candidate whose declared unit matches that prefix can likewise retain the amount. Require the captured denominator to equal a supported unit rather than merely start with one.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fold traditional date wrappers during event alignment**

The scorer allows simplified date boundaries around an inner event anchor but not their traditional equivalents. With an anchor on `2026年1月`, `從2026年1月起` resolves as `unregistered_position` while `从2026年1月起` aligns, and `2026年1月後` similarly fails while `...后` aligns. Production accepts these traditional date forms, so the experiment incorrectly records otherwise equivalent predictions as an FP plus FN; fold `從`/`後`/`間` only in this containment check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop attaching layout guards across unrelated blocks**

Beyond the separately bounded lexical-continuation path, this layout view still concatenates every earlier and later block, including different pages, before applying range, qualifier, arithmetic, and rate guards. I reproduced a valid `王甲收到工资4000元` on page 1 being downgraded to `approximate`, `range`, or `unsupported` when an unrelated page-2 block began with `以上事实无争议`, `至5000元为李乙工资`, or `×2是附件编号`. Restrict these continuations to a demonstrably contiguous OCR fragment or the same local event.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject currency-prefixed labels that contain no amount**

Any occurrence of `人民币` or a currency symbol makes the whole value monetary before the complete no-amount wage-label grammar runs. Consequently `人民币工资`, `人民币薪资`, `人民币金额`, and `￥工资` are retained as accepted money candidates with `unsupported` normalization; I also reproduced `王甲人民币工资` being accepted with no review issue. Classify complete currency-plus-label phrases without a numeral or masked amount as `not_monetary`, while retaining genuinely unknown monetary expressions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat conjunction-linked suffixes as bounds**

When `以上` or `以下` is introduced by the common conjunctions `及` or `或`, this suffix grammar no longer attaches the qualifier to the amount. Both `normalizeMoneyValueV4('4000元及以上')` and a cropped `4000元` candidate quoted from `王甲工资4000元或以下` return `exact` with `4000.00`, so a lower or upper bound can become an exact production amount. Allow the bounded conjunction before these suffixes while retaining the existing ordinary-prose continuation guards.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept 个月 as a monthly rate denominator**

Common monthly-rate forms using the explicit classifier `个`, such as `4000元每个月` and `4000元/个月` (and traditional `每個月`), are classified as unsupported because the captured denominator must begin directly with `月`. The otherwise equivalent `4000元每月` and `4000元/月` remain exact, so a valid candidate declared with `meaning: "rate"` and `rateUnit: "month"` loses its amount solely because of this ordinary unit spelling. Recognize the complete `个月`/`個月` alias without accepting longer words such as `月份` or `月亮`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
